text:
The best match for the farm's future climate in the 2050s is Walla Walla County, Washington, which has a strong match quality, with all 8 climate models agreeing. Sigma measures how different a place's climate today is from the farm's future climate, in units of the farm's normal year-to-year swings, where lower means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Regarding rotations, 2 matching areas use the field's current rotation of a flexible mix of pulses, spring wheat, and winter wheat. Other rotations used at the matching places include winter wheat going to fallow, a flexible mix of fallow, pulses, and winter wheat, and a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, and winter wheat.

Comparing the farm to the best match, the best match has 37 days above 32 degrees Celsius per year compared to the field's 27, and 211 frost-free days compared to the field's 172. The afternoon ground temperature in June is 35.7 degrees Celsius at the match and 30.5 at the field, while in July and August it is 46.5 degrees Celsius at the match and 42.1 at the field. For the driest month soil water percentage, September is 17.8 at the match and 18.1 at the field.

Climate projections for the future indicate that temperatures will rise across all seasons, and precipitation will change across the year. 

These results are based on candidates from 3351 farmland cells at approximately 4 kilometers using the Cropland Data Layer.
